S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

info.persona: Maria Fuentes blends razor‑sharp audit instincts with a relentless love for salsa dancing, juggling spreadsheets and salsa steps while secretly hoarding an ever‑growing collection of artisanal coffee beans that often spill onto her audit reports.
info.professional_persona: Maria Fuentes, a seasoned accounting professional with expertise in GAAP compliance, financial statement analysis, and AI‑enhanced audit tools, channels her competitive drive and skeptical eye into rigorous fraud detection while mentoring junior staff with an unconventional, flexible project‑management style.
info.cultural_background: Maria grew up in a bicultural Mexican‑American household, speaking both Spanish and English at home. Her family maintains strong ties to Mexican traditions, celebrating Día de los Muertos, quinceañeras, and Semana Santa with community gatherings that blend religious devotion and vibrant cultural expression. Living in Lawndale, she is part of a tight‑knit Latino community that values family, mutual support, and collective celebration. These roots influence her warm, sociable demeanor and her commitment to giving back through cultural events and mentorship of other Hispanic women entering the accounting profession.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outside of work, Maria is an avid supporter of the arts and community life. She frequents local galleries and museums, often drawing creative inspiration for her cooking and photography. She participates in salsa and cumbia dance classes, enjoys hiking the coastal trails of Southern California with friends, and volunteers at the neighborhood cultural center where she helps organize events celebrating Mexican heritage. Maria also reads contemporary fiction and business strategy books, and experiments with modern twists on traditional Mexican recipes.
info.sports_persona: Maria Fuentes fuels her fitness by hiking the rugged coastal trails with the Southern California Trailblazers club, playing weekly co‑ed tennis at the La Jolla Racquet Club, and cheering for the Los Angeles Dodgers and the LA Lakers, while her competitive streak pushes her to sign up for the annual LA Marathon despite a demanding work schedule.
info.arts_persona: Maria Fuentes cultivates her artistic side by frequenting LACMA to study works by Frida Kahlo and Yayoi Kusama, attending live performances of the LA Philharmonic featuring Yo‑Yo Ma, and drawing culinary inspiration from the vibrant rhythms of Celia Cruz and the cinematic storytelling of Guillermo del Toro.
info.travel_persona: Maria Fuentes plans trips with meticulous spreadsheets, blending weekend getaways to Santa Barbara’s vineyards with longer sojourns to Barcelona’s historic quarters, Lisbon’s riverfront neighborhoods, and Sedona’s red‑rock canyons, balancing her love for cultural immersion with a need for coastal hikes that soothe her stress.
info.culinary_persona: Maria Fuentes, an avid home chef, reinvents classic dishes like grilled corn esquites with smoked paprika and cotija, quinoa‑topped chorizo tacos, and mole‑infused dark chocolate ramen, showcasing her skillful use of roasted tomatillos, chipotle, and fresh cilantro to fuse tradition with modern gastronomy.

info.persona: Dennis Schwarting is a 57‑year‑old call‑center veteran who balances curiosity with practicality, lives for community‑rooted brews and lake walks, and constantly wrestles with deadline‑driven stress and spontaneous habits, often reassuring themselves that they can still find balance.
info.professional_persona: Dennis Schwarting, an experienced call‑center veteran, blends two decades of frontline problem‑solving with a curiosity for new service tools, using their strong listening and CRM expertise (Salesforce, Zendesk) to coach peers while often battling the same deadline‑driven stress that fuels their spontaneous, hands‑on leadership style.
info.cultural_background: Dennis comes from a multigenerational working‑class family in Milwaukee with German‑Polish ancestry. He grew up in a neighborhood where community emphasized hard work, modesty, and neighborly support—values typical of the Midwest. Traditional celebrations such as German Oktoberfest and St. Pat’s influenced his appreciation for local brews and communal gatherings. His upbringing in a Catholic‑leaning household taught him a sense of responsibility and service, which translates into his compassionate yet practical approach at work. The region’s strong sports culture (Milwaukee Brewers, Green Bay Packers) and love of the Great Lakes also shape his leisure activities and identity.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Dennis enjoys a blend of solitary and social pastimes that reflect his Midwestern roots and his need for both relaxation and connection. On weekends, he often heads to Lake Michigan’s shoreline for fishing or a leisurely walk, finding the quiet waters a perfect antidote to work‑related stress. He is an avid patron of local breweries, enjoying casual beer‑tasting sessions with friends and colleagues, and he occasionally participates in community events like Milwaukee Summerfest or the local Oktoberfest celebration. At home, Dennis dabbles in DIY home‑improvement projects and tends a small vegetable garden, activities that satisfy his curiosity for practical problem‑solving. He also reads mystery novels and technology magazines, and volunteers a few hours each month at a community center, helping seniors navigate digital services.
info.sports_persona: Dennis Schwarting follows the Milwaukee Brewers and Green Bay Packers with fervor, joins a local walking club for weekend lakeside strolls, grabs a paddleboard at Lake Michigan in summer, but their flexible schedule means gym visits are sporadic, and they often trade a planned run for an impromptu fishing trip.
info.arts_persona: Dennis Schwarting enjoys mystery novels by Agatha Christie and technology magazines, attends occasional performances by the Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra, shares a love for classic rock icons like The Rolling Stones and local folk bands at beer‑tasting events, and they flexibly squeeze in a crossword puzzle during quiet evenings.
info.travel_persona: Dennis Schwarting prefers road‑trip escapes to Door County’s vineyards and the Upper Peninsula’s lighthouses, has taken a nostalgic pilgrimage to Dublin for St. Patrick’s Day, dreams of a leisurely cruise on Lake Michigan’s historic vessels, yet their spontaneous planning habit often leaves travel dates open to last‑minute changes, and they frequently end up booking flights just a few weeks in advance.
info.culinary_persona: Dennis Schwarting delights in grilling fresh lake trout, simmering hearty bratwurst with sauerkraut, and tossing home‑grown tomatoes into a rustic gazpacho, proudly pairing the meals with locally brewed IPAs, but their DIY kitchen projects sometimes lead to a cluttered pantry and they have a tendency to forget to freeze leftovers.

info.persona: Janet Kinkaid is a structured, community‑driven senior who balances meticulous planning with a love for gardening, quilting, and lively bridge games, yet occasionally overcommits to volunteer projects and forgets to take their daily vitamins.
info.professional_persona: Janet Kinkaid, a retired senior center coordinator with a knack for meticulous event planning, budget oversight, and volunteer logistics, now channels their methodical, sociable leadership into expanding outreach programs, launching a neighborhood garden, and preserving local history through oral interviews.
info.cultural_background: Janet grew up in the heart of Middle Tennessee, steeped in Southern traditions of hospitality, family, and church life. Her upbringing in a close‑knit, predominantly white community emphasized community service, respect for elders, and a love of regional cuisine and music. She maintains strong ties to her local Methodist congregation, participates in county fairs, and values the preservation of local history and customs. While honoring these roots, she adapts them by fostering inclusive, intergenerational programs that reflect contemporary values.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Janet enjoys a blend of social and creative pursuits. She spends time gardening, especially heirloom vegetables, and shares recipes in her church’s cooking club. She is an active member of a book club focused on historical fiction, participates in the church choir, and loves knitting quilts for charity. Weekends often find her at bridge tables in the senior center, walking local trails, or researching her family genealogy at the county library.
info.sports_persona: Janet Kinkaid enjoys low‑impact fitness, walking the local Natchez Trace trails three times a week, participates in the senior center’s pickleball league, and cheers passionately for the Tennessee Titans on Sundays, balancing an active routine with regular rest to protect their joints.
info.arts_persona: Janet Kinkaid blends creative expression and cultural appreciation by quilting historical patterns for charity, singing in the church choir with a fondness for gospel classics and the hymns of Mahalia Jackson, devouring historical fiction by Philippa Gregory, and attending the Nashville Symphony’s occasional performances of Beethoven’s Ninth, all while sharing their love of the arts with fellow community members.
info.travel_persona: Janet Kinkaid plans travel with meticulous lists, preferring relaxed, historically rich trips such as a guided tour of the Great Smoky Mountains, a weekend exploring Colonial Williamsburg, and a pilgrimage to the Civil War battlefield sites in Tennessee, while budgeting carefully and often inviting their grandchildren to join for intergenerational learning.
info.culinary_persona: Janet Kinkaid delights in cooking heirloom vegetable dishes like roasted beet and sweet‑potato salad with fresh dill, bakes cornbread and banana pudding for the church’s cooking club, and confidently posts recipes on community Facebook pages, all while maintaining a modest kitchen skill level that flourishes when experimenting with new herbs like thyme and rosemary.
